topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: How many members serve on the Tennessee Real Estate Commission?
choice_a: Seven members
choice_b: Nine members
choice_c: Eleven members
choice_d: Five members
explanation: T.C.A. § 62-13-201 creates a nine-member commission appointed by the governor.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under T.C.A. § 62-13-201, how are the nine seats on the Tennessee Real Estate Commission divided?
choice_a: Five industry members and four public members
choice_b: All nine members must be actively licensed brokers
choice_c: Seven members who have been licensed brokers or affiliate brokers for at least five years, and two members not engaged in real estate brokerage, financing, or development
choice_d: Six industry members and three members representing consumer advocacy groups
explanation: Seven members must have five years' experience as a licensed broker or affiliate broker; the remaining two must not be engaged in real estate brokerage, financing, or development.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: How must the nine Commission seats be geographically distributed among Tennessee's grand divisions?
choice_a: Members are apportioned solely by county population
choice_b: At least five members must reside in Nashville
choice_c: There is no geographic distribution requirement
choice_d: Three members from each of the eastern, middle, and western grand divisions
explanation: T.C.A. § 62-13-201 requires three members appointed from each of the state's three grand divisions.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What is the length of a term for a Tennessee Real Estate Commission member?
choice_a: Five years
choice_b: Four years
choice_c: Three years
choice_d: Six years
explanation: Commission members are appointed for five-year terms under T.C.A. § 62-13-201.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under T.C.A. § 62-13-201, may a Commission member be reappointed to serve more than one full consecutive term?
choice_a: Yes, members may serve unlimited consecutive terms
choice_b: No, a member may not be appointed to succeed themselves for more than one full term
choice_c: Yes, but only up to three consecutive terms
choice_d: Reappointment is allowed only for the two public members
explanation: The statute limits a member to one full term of consecutive reappointment.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: On what grounds may the governor remove a Commission member under T.C.A. § 62-13-201?
choice_a: Only a felony conviction
choice_b: Missing two consecutive meetings
choice_c: Misconduct, incompetency, or willful neglect of duty
choice_d: The statute provides no removal mechanism
explanation: The governor may remove a member for misconduct, incompetency, or willful neglect of duty, filling the vacancy for the unexpired term.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What protection does T.C.A. § 62-13-202 provide regarding the Commission's disciplinary actions?
choice_a: Commission members may be personally sued for any disciplinary decision
choice_b: The Commission has no protection from liability
choice_c: Only the executive director is immune from liability, not the commissioners
choice_d: The Commission acts as a judicial body when disciplining licensees, which shields it and its members from related civil liability
explanation: Section 62-13-202 designates the commission as a judicial body for these purposes, insulating it from civil liability arising from its official acts.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: How does the Tennessee Real Estate Commission select its leadership under T.C.A. § 62-13-203?
choice_a: The commission organizes itself by selecting a chair and vice chair from among its own members
choice_b: The governor appoints the chair directly
choice_c: The executive director automatically serves as chair
choice_d: Leadership rotates monthly among all nine members
explanation: The commission organizes by electing a chair and vice chair from among its members.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under what legal framework must the Tennessee Real Estate Commission promulgate its rules?
choice_a: The Tennessee Rules of Civil Procedure
choice_b: The Uniform Administrative Procedures Act (T.C.A. Title 4, Chapter 5)
choice_c: The federal Administrative Procedure Act
choice_d: There is no formal process; the Commission may issue rules at will
explanation: Section 62-13-203 requires rulemaking to proceed under the Uniform Administrative Procedures Act.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: T.C.A. § 62-13-203 authorizes the Commission's rules to establish which of the following?
choice_a: Criminal penalties for licensees exceeding those set by statute
choice_b: Property tax rates for real estate transactions
choice_c: Canons of ethics and minimum standards of practice for licensees
choice_d: Federal fair housing enforcement procedures
explanation: Among its rulemaking powers, the commission may adopt canons of ethics and minimum acceptable standards of practice.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under T.C.A. § 62-13-204, what is the Commission expressly prohibited from doing?
choice_a: Approving continuing education providers
choice_b: Issuing licenses to qualified applicants
choice_c: Investigating consumer complaints
choice_d: Setting fees or commissions for real estate contracts or transactions
explanation: Section 62-13-204 bars the commission from setting or controlling fees or commissions charged in real estate transactions.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What consequence does T.C.A. § 62-13-204 impose if the Commission is found to have actually set or controlled fees or commissions for real estate transactions?
choice_a: All members of the Commission forfeit their licenses
choice_b: The Commission is dissolved and reconstituted by the legislature
choice_c: The Governor must personally review every transaction
choice_d: No consequence is specified; it is only advisory
explanation: If that practice is found to occur in actual practice due to Commission action, all commission members forfeit their licenses.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What qualification does T.C.A. § 62-13-207 require of the Commission's executive director?
choice_a: The executive director must be a sitting Commission member
choice_b: The executive director must have successfully completed the Tennessee broker's examination
choice_c: The executive director must hold a law degree
choice_d: There is no qualification requirement for the executive director
explanation: The executive director must have passed the Tennessee broker's examination, with other qualifications set by the commission.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What is the term length for the Commission's executive director under T.C.A. § 62-13-207?
choice_a: Two years, non-renewable
choice_b: A lifetime appointment
choice_c: Four years, with eligibility for reappointment
choice_d: One year, renewable annually only once
explanation: The executive director serves a four-year term and may be reappointed.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What qualification does T.C.A. § 62-13-207 require of the Commission's director of education?
choice_a: A current real estate broker's license only
choice_b: A law degree and bar admission
choice_c: No formal education requirement, only ten years of industry experience
choice_d: A college degree from an accredited university, in a full-time position
explanation: The commission must employ a full-time director of education holding a college degree from an accredited university.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What is the general purpose of the real estate education and recovery account established under T.C.A. § 62-13-208?
choice_a: To compensate persons who suffer monetary damage as a result of violations of the Tennessee Real Estate Broker License Act by a licensee
choice_b: To fund the Commission's general operating budget
choice_c: To pay for Commission members' travel expenses
choice_d: To provide scholarships for real estate students
explanation: The fund exists to compensate members of the public aggrieved by violations of the Act.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: How is the real estate education and recovery account primarily funded under T.C.A. § 62-13-208?
choice_a: Exclusively through general state tax revenue
choice_b: Through fees paid by original license applicants and an assessment that may be added to renewal fees
choice_c: Through fines paid by consumers who file frivolous complaints
choice_d: Through federal HUD grants
explanation: Original applicants pay a commission-set fee into the account, and renewal fees may include an assessment to maintain the required minimum balance.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What is the maximum amount that may be paid from the recovery account for a single claim (transaction) under T.C.A. § 62-13-208?
explanation: The statute caps payment on any one claim at $15,000, regardless of how many parties or properties are involved.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What is the maximum aggregate amount the recovery account will pay arising from the actions of any one licensee under T.C.A. § 62-13-208?
choice_c: There is no aggregate cap, only a per-claim cap
explanation: The fund's liability for payments arising from a single licensee's conduct terminates once aggregate payments reach $30,000.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What minimum balance must the Commission maintain in the real estate education and recovery account under T.C.A. § 62-13-208?
explanation: The commission is required to maintain a $500,000 floor balance in the account, assessing renewal fees as needed to keep it funded.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: If the recovery account pays a claim arising from a licensee's conduct, what must that licensee do to have a suspended or revoked license reinstated under T.C.A. § 62-13-208?
choice_a: Nothing; the license is automatically reinstated after one year
choice_b: Repay the amount paid from the account, plus interest at the account's effective earnings rate
choice_c: Complete only an additional 8 hours of continuing education
choice_d: File a personal bankruptcy discharge covering the debt
explanation: Reinstatement requires the licensee to repay the account in full, plus interest at the account's effective earnings rate.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under T.C.A. § 62-13-312(a), how may the Commission initiate a disciplinary investigation?
choice_a: Only after a criminal conviction has already occurred
choice_b: Only at the request of the Governor's office
choice_c: On its own motion, or upon a verified written complaint from any person
choice_d: Only when referred by a Tennessee district attorney
explanation: The commission may act on its own motion and must act on a verified written complaint, ascertaining the facts before deciding whether a hearing is warranted.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under T.C.A. § 62-13-312(b), what disciplinary exposure does a principal broker face for failing to properly oversee an affiliate broker?
choice_a: A broker cannot be disciplined for an affiliate's conduct under any circumstance
choice_b: Only the affiliate broker, never the supervising broker, may be disciplined
choice_c: Supervision failures may only be addressed through civil lawsuits, not Commission discipline
choice_d: Failing to exercise adequate supervision over the activities of any licensed affiliate brokers is itself listed as grounds for discipline against the supervising licensee
explanation: Section 62-13-312(b) lists a licensee's failure to exercise adequate supervision over affiliate brokers as an independent ground for discipline.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: T.C.A. § 62-13-312(b) makes it a disciplinary violation for a broker to fail to do what regarding an affiliate broker who transfers or is terminated?
choice_a: Complete, within a reasonable time, the administrative measures required by the Commission upon the transfer or termination
choice_b: Pay the departing affiliate broker's final commission within 24 hours
choice_c: Notify the affiliate broker's new employer of any pending litigation
choice_d: Refund the affiliate broker's original licensing fee
explanation: Failing within a reasonable time to complete the administrative measures the commission requires upon an affiliate broker's transfer or termination is a listed ground for discipline.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Which conduct is specifically listed as grounds for discipline under T.C.A. § 62-13-312(b)?
choice_a: Hiring more than five affiliate brokers at one time
choice_b: Pursuing a continued and flagrant course of misrepresentation or false promises through affiliate brokers, other persons, or any advertising medium
choice_c: Advertising a property without an MLS listing
choice_d: Failing to renew a firm's business license with the county
explanation: This is one of the enumerated grounds for discipline in section 62-13-312(b).

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: T.C.A. § 62-13-312(b) lists which of the following as an independent ground for license discipline?
choice_a: Failing to attend the Commission's annual conference
choice_b: Advertising on more than one real estate website
choice_c: Violating any federal, state, or municipal law prohibiting discrimination in the sale or rental of real estate
choice_d: Declining to work weekends
explanation: Violating a fair housing or anti-discrimination law is expressly listed as grounds for discipline.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: T.C.A. § 62-13-312(b) contains a catch-all provision covering which conduct?
choice_a: Only conduct that has already resulted in a criminal conviction
choice_b: Conduct occurring exclusively during business hours
choice_c: Only conduct involving out-of-state transactions
choice_d: Any conduct, of the same or a different character than the other listed grounds, that constitutes improper, fraudulent, or dishonest dealing
explanation: The statute's catch-all clause reaches any improper, fraudulent, or dishonest dealing, whether or not it matches the other enumerated grounds.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Instead of suspending or revoking a broker's license, what alternative disciplinary measure does T.C.A. § 62-13-312(c) allow the Commission to impose?
choice_a: Downgrading the broker to affiliate broker status
choice_b: Requiring the broker to pay double the original licensing fee
choice_c: Transferring the broker's license to a different grand division
choice_d: Requiring the broker to work exclusively under Commission supervision for one year
explanation: As an alternative or additional remedy, the commission may order a broker downgraded to affiliate broker status.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under T.C.A. § 62-13-312(f), what happens to a licensee's license if they are convicted of certain crimes and fail to request a hearing?
choice_a: The license remains valid indefinitely until a civil suit is filed
choice_b: The license is automatically revoked 60 days after the conviction
choice_c: Only a written warning is issued
choice_d: The Commission must wait five years before taking any action
explanation: A convicted licensee must notify the commission within 60 days, and the license is automatically revoked at that point unless a hearing is requested.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What collateral effect does a licensee's suspension or license surrender have under T.C.A. § 62-13-312(g) if that person also holds school or instructor approval?
choice_a: The school or instructor approval is unaffected
choice_b: The Commission must issue a new instructor license automatically
choice_c: The related school or instructor approval is also revoked
choice_d: Only the Department of Education can revoke instructor status, not TREC
explanation: A suspension or surrender of the underlying license triggers revocation of any associated school or instructor approval.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: How many days does a licensee or applicant have to file a written answer after the Commission notifies them of a complaint, under T.C.A. § 62-13-313?
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 60 days
choice_c: 5 days
choice_d: 10 days
explanation: The commission must notify the accused party in writing, who then has 10 days to file an answer.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What vote threshold does T.C.A. § 62-13-313 require for the Commission to revoke or suspend a license?
choice_a: An affirmative vote of a majority of the Commission
choice_b: A unanimous vote of all nine members
choice_c: A two-thirds supermajority
choice_d: Approval by the Governor alone
explanation: A license may be revoked or suspended only upon an affirmative majority vote of the commission.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under T.C.A. § 62-13-313, within what general timeframe must a disciplinary complaint be filed?
choice_a: Exactly 90 days from the violation, with no exceptions
choice_b: The longer of two years from the violation (or its discovery), the applicable criminal statute of limitations, or ten days after conclusion of a related criminal prosecution
choice_c: There is no time limit for filing a complaint
choice_d: Complaints must be filed within 30 days of licensing renewal
explanation: The statute sets a filing deadline keyed to whichever of these three periods is longest.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under T.C.A. § 62-13-311, what may a Tennessee court do as part of a civil judgment against a licensee for gross negligence, incompetency, fraud, dishonesty, or misconduct?
choice_a: Order the Commission to pay the plaintiff's damages
choice_b: Automatically transfer the license to the plaintiff
choice_c: Revoke the licensee's certificate of license as part of its judgment or decree
choice_d: Suspend the licenses of all brokers in the same firm
explanation: When a court enters judgment against a licensee for such conduct, it may, as part of that judgment, revoke the license.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Following a court-ordered license revocation under T.C.A. § 62-13-311, how may the license be reissued?
choice_a: Automatically after one year with no Commission action
choice_b: Only through a new act of the state legislature
choice_c: The license may never be reissued under any circumstance
choice_d: Only upon the consenting vote of six Commission members in favor of reissuance
explanation: Reissuance after a court-ordered revocation requires the affirmative consenting vote of six commission members.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What administrative role does the Commission play regarding errors and omissions insurance under T.C.A. § 62-13-112?
choice_a: The Commission contracts with insurance providers through competitive bidding and establishes minimum coverage terms, limits, and deductibles
choice_b: The Commission has no involvement; E&O insurance is purely a private matter between licensee and insurer
choice_c: The Commission directly underwrites all E&O policies itself
choice_d: The Commission only regulates E&O insurance for firms, not individual licensees
explanation: The commission administers the E&O program by competitively bidding a provider contract and setting minimum coverage terms, though licensees may also obtain independent policies meeting those minimums.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What happens to a licensee's license under T.C.A. § 62-13-112 if they fail to maintain required errors and omissions insurance?
choice_a: Nothing; E&O insurance is optional in Tennessee
choice_b: The license is suspended, with escalating penalties and eventual automatic revocation if the lapse exceeds one year
choice_c: The license is immediately and permanently revoked with no reinstatement option
choice_d: Only a formal written reprimand is issued
explanation: Noncompliance results in suspension, escalating monetary penalties the longer the lapse continues, and automatic revocation if the suspension exceeds one year.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What authority does the Commission hold over individuals who teach real estate continuing education courses, per T.C.A. § 62-13-324?
choice_a: Continuing education instructors are licensed exclusively by the Department of Education, not TREC
choice_b: Any licensed broker may teach continuing education without Commission approval
choice_c: The Commission approves and regulates real estate continuing education instructors
choice_d: The Commission has no role in continuing education instruction
explanation: Section 62-13-324 gives the commission authority over the approval of continuing education instructors.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under T.C.A. § 62-13-325, what must occur before a distance education course may satisfy a licensee's education requirement?
choice_a: Distance education courses are categorically prohibited from satisfying licensing requirements
choice_b: Only courses offered by out-of-state universities qualify
choice_c: No approval is required as long as the course is at least one hour long
choice_d: The distance education course must be approved by the Commission
explanation: Distance education courses must receive Commission approval to count toward a licensee's education requirement.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Besides adopting rules, what enforcement power does T.C.A. § 62-13-203 give the Commission?
choice_a: The Commission may take necessary legal steps through the proper legal officer to enforce the chapter and collect penalties for violations
choice_b: The Commission may impose criminal jail sentences directly
choice_c: The Commission may seize a licensee's personal property without judicial process
choice_d: The Commission has no enforcement power beyond issuing warnings
explanation: The commission may pursue enforcement of the chapter and collection of penalties through the proper legal officer.
